findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify AC4's reclaim mechanism lifecycle: what triggers it, that it cannot run concurrently with (or races safely against) build bursts, and that it is idempotent under repeated/overlapping triggers.
evidence: AC4: 'a mechanism that cannot exceed a configured high-water mark regardless of build burst rate'
Chronology: Aug-4 fix was 'pressure-triggered docker prune on the autodeploy no-op tick' — a prior reclaim trigger with no stated ownership/concurrency
'Reclaim has been made faster and more triggered each round, but nothing has ever bounded the CEILING' — implies multiple overlapping triggers
findings.finding: AC4 introduces a bounded high-water-mark reclaim mechanism on the host but does not specify its lifecycle/concurrency: who triggers it, whether concurrent build bursts can race the reclaim (check-then-prune TOCTOU), and whether it is idempotent under repeated triggers. The prior mitigations were pressure-triggered docker prunes on the autodeploy no-op tick, which is exactly the kind of unbounded-trigger state whose ownership matters.
findings.location: AC4 (root usage has a bounded CEILING)
scenarios: A build burst writes faster than a single-shot prune runs, and two triggers (autodeploy tick + pressure threshold) fire concurrently, either double-pruning live layers or racing so neither bounds the peak
findings.suggested_fix: State the reclaim trigger and ownership (e.g. a single serialized enforcer keyed on the high-water mark, guarded so concurrent invocations coalesce), and note it is idempotent so overlapping triggers cannot over- or under-prune.

findings.checklist_item: State that the AC1/AC2 treat_missing_data change is made in the Terraform alarm resources and rolled out via plan/apply (with `describe-alarms` as post-apply verification), not via an out-of-band console/CLI edit.
evidence: AC1: 'Verified by `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` showing the new setting'
The alarms are IaC-managed: infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf defines aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.root_disk_pressure and monitoring.tf defines .gerrit_data_disk_high
T10 checklist: 'Remote state + locking; plan-before-apply discipline' and 'Changes idempotent; drift / out-of-band manual changes considered'
findings.finding: AC1/AC2 change the durable CloudWatch alarm configuration (treat_missing_data) but specify only CLI verification (`aws cloudwatch describe-alarms`), never stating the change is applied through Terraform plan/apply on the managed resources (aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.root_disk_pressure / .gerrit_data_disk_high). An out-of-band console/CLI edit would drift from state and be reverted on the next apply.
scenarios: An operator edits the alarm via console/CLI to satisfy AC1; the next terraform apply reverts treat_missing_data back to notBreaching, silently reopening the dead-man's-switch inversion.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC1/AC2: change treat_missing_data in the aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm resources (monitoring_autodeploy.tf, monitoring.tf) and apply via terraform plan/apply; use `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` only to confirm the applied state, not as the change mechanism.

findings.checklist_item: Add a step (or AC) to reconcile the out-of-band 30->60 GiB root volume size back into IaC/user_data so the resize does not remain as untracked drift.
evidence: '`modify-volume` root 30 -> 60 GiB'
AC6 documents 'snapshot -> modify-volume -> reboot -> cloud-init growpart' as an unwedge but does not require reconciling the new size back into IaC
T10 checklist: 'Changes idempotent; drift / out-of-band manual changes considered'
findings.finding: Recovery grew the root EBS volume out-of-band (`modify-volume` 30 -> 60 GiB) but the plan does not reconcile the new size into IaC (e.g. the volume/user_data or instance root_block_device definition). If the root volume size is Terraform-managed, the next apply will show drift and could try to change/replace it; AC6 records the unwedge as a runbook step without a state-reconciliation step.
scenarios: The 60 GiB volume drifts from a Terraform root_block_device volume_size that still says 30; a future apply reports the diff or attempts a size/instance change.
findings.suggested_fix: Note in the plan whether the root volume size is Terraform-managed; if so, update the managed volume_size to 60 GiB and apply, or explicitly document why it is intentionally unmanaged.
